passages.text: This is the burden that Habakkuk the prophet received in a vision: How long, O LORD, must I call for help but You do not hear, or cry out to You, “Violence!” but You do not save?
passages.sermon:
Habakkuk was a prophet.
\r\nGod gave Habakkuk a vision.
\r\nThis vision was a burden for Habakkuk.
\r\nHabakkuk spoke to the LORD.
\r\nHabakkuk called for help.
\r\nThe LORD did not answer.
\r\nHabakkuk cried out to God about violence.
\r\nGod did not save.
passages.original: הַמַּשָׂא֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה חֲבַקּ֖וּק הַנָּבִֽיא׃ עַד־ אָ֧נָה יְהוָ֛ה שִׁוַּ֖עְתִּי וְלֹ֣א תִשְׁמָ֑ע אֶזְעַ֥ק אֵלֶ֛יךָ חָמָ֖ס וְלֹ֥א תוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

passages.text: Why do You make me see iniquity? Why do You tolerate wrongdoing? Destruction and violence are before me. Strife is ongoing, and conflict abounds.
passages.sermon:
Habakkuk is a prophet.
Habakkuk speaks to God.
Habakkuk asks God a question.
Habakkuk says, “Why do You make me see iniquity?”
Habakkuk asks, “Why do You tolerate wrongdoing?”
Habakkuk sees destruction in front of him.
Habakkuk sees violence before him.
Strife is always present.
Conflict is everywhere.
passages.original: לָ֣מָּה תַרְאֵ֤נִי אָ֙וֶן֙ וְעָמָ֣ל תַּבִּ֔יט וְשֹׁ֥ד וְחָמָ֖ס לְנֶגְדִּ֑י וַיְהִ֧י רִ֦יב וּמָד֖וֹן יִשָּֽׂא׃

passages.text: Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted.
passages.sermon:
Habakkuk is a prophet.
Habakkuk received a vision from God.
Habakkuk saw that the law became powerless.
Justice did not come forth.
Wicked people surrounded righteous people.
Wicked people trapped the righteous.
Because of this, justice became twisted.
Justice was no longer true.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּן֙ תָּפ֣וּג תּוֹרָ֔ה וְלֹֽא־ יֵצֵ֥א לָנֶ֖צַח מִשְׁפָּ֑ט כִּ֤י רָשָׁע֙ מַכְתִּ֣יר אֶת־ הַצַּדִּ֔יק עַל־ כֵּ֛ן יֵצֵ֥א מִשְׁפָּ֖ט מְעֻקָּֽל׃

passages.text: “Look at the nations and observe— be utterly astounded! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe even if someone told you.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people.
God tells them to look at the nations.
God commands them to observe what is happening.
God says they will be utterly astounded.
God declares He is doing a work in their days.
God says this work is unbelievable.
God says they would not believe it even if someone told them.
passages.original: רְא֤וּ בַגּוֹיִם֙ וְֽהַבִּ֔יטוּ וְהִֽתַּמְּה֖וּ תְּמָ֑הוּ כִּי־ פֹ֙עַל֙ פֹּעֵ֣ל בִּֽימֵיכֶ֔ם לֹ֥א תַאֲמִ֖ינוּ כִּ֥י יְסֻפָּֽר׃

passages.text: For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans — that ruthless and impetuous nation which marches through the breadth of the earth to seize dwellings not their own.
passages.sermon:
God speaks in this passage.
God says, “I am raising up the Chaldeans.”
The Chaldeans are a nation.
They are ruthless.
They are impetuous.
They move quickly and act without restraint.
They march across the whole earth.
They go to places far from their own land.
They seize homes that do not belong to them.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ הִנְנִ֤י מֵקִים֙ אֶת־ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים הַגּ֖וֹי הַמַּ֣ר וְהַנִּמְהָ֑ר הַֽהוֹלֵךְ֙ לְמֶרְחֲבֵי־ אֶ֔רֶץ לָרֶ֖שֶׁת מִשְׁכָּנ֥וֹת לֹּא־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: They are dreaded and feared; from themselves they derive justice and sovereignty.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans are a ruthless and impetuous nation.
People dread and fear them.
They decide their own justice.
They hold their own power.
Their authority comes from themselves.
passages.original: אָיֹ֥ם וְנוֹרָ֖א ה֑וּא מִמֶּ֕נּוּ מִשְׁפָּט֥וֹ וּשְׂאֵת֖וֹ יֵצֵֽא׃

passages.text: Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves of the night. Their horsemen charge ahead, and their cavalry comes from afar. They fly like a vulture, swooping down to devour.
passages.sermon:
The Chaldeans are a ruthless and impetuous nation.
Their horses run faster than leopards.
Their horses are fiercer than wolves that hunt at night.
Their horsemen rush forward quickly.
Their cavalry comes from distant places.
They fly swiftly like a vulture.
They swoop down to devour.
passages.original: וְקַלּ֨וּ מִנְּמֵרִ֜ים סוּסָ֗יו וְחַדּוּ֙ מִזְּאֵ֣בֵי עֶ֔רֶב וּפָ֖שׁוּ פָּֽרָשָׁ֑יו וּפָֽרָשָׁיו֙ מֵרָח֣וֹק יָבֹ֔אוּ יָעֻ֕פוּ כְּנֶ֖שֶׁר חָ֥שׁ לֶאֱכֽוֹל׃

passages.text: All of them come bent on violence; their hordes advance like the east wind; they gather prisoners like sand.
passages.sermon:
The people in this passage are the Babylonians.
The Babylonians come to attack.
They want to do violence.
They move forward quickly.
They advance like the east wind.
They take many prisoners.
They gather prisoners as easily as someone gathers sand.
passages.original: כֻּלֹּה֙ לְחָמָ֣ס יָב֔וֹא מְגַמַּ֥ת פְּנֵיהֶ֖ם קָדִ֑ימָה וַיֶּאֱסֹ֥ף כַּח֖וֹל שֶֽׁבִי׃

passages.text: They scoff at kings and make rulers an object of scorn. They laugh at every fortress and build up siege ramps to seize it.
passages.sermon:
The Babylonians are a fierce and powerful nation.
They show no respect for kings.
They mock rulers.
They laugh at every fortress.
They build up dirt ramps against strongholds.
They capture every city they attack.
passages.original: וְהוּא֙ בַּמְּלָכִ֣ים יִתְקַלָּ֔ס וְרֹזְנִ֖ים מִשְׂחָ֣ק ל֑וֹ ה֚וּא לְכָל־ מִבְצָ֣ר יִשְׂחָ֔ק וַיִּצְבֹּ֥ר עָפָ֖ר וַֽיִּלְכְּדָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Then they sweep by like the wind and pass on through. They are guilty; their own strength is their god.”
passages.sermon:
The people move quickly.
They sweep by like the wind.
They pass through the land.
They are guilty.
They trust in their own strength.
They treat their own power as their god.
passages.original: אָ֣ז חָלַ֥ף ר֛וּחַ וַֽיַּעֲבֹ֖ר וְאָשֵׁ֑ם ז֥וּ כֹח֖וֹ לֵאלֹהֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Are You not from everlasting, O LORD, my God, my Holy One? We will not die. O LORD, You have appointed them to execute judgment; O Rock, You have established them for correction.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Habakkuk speaks to God.
God is everlasting.
God is the LORD.
God is my God.
God is the Holy One.
We will not die.
God, You have appointed them to bring judgment.
God, You are the Rock.
You have established them to correct us.
passages.original: הֲל֧וֹא אַתָּ֣ה מִקֶּ֗דֶם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛י קְדֹשִׁ֖י לֹ֣א נָמ֑וּת יְהוָה֙ לְמִשְׁפָּ֣ט שַׂמְתּ֔וֹ וְצ֖וּר לְהוֹכִ֥יחַ יְסַדְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Your eyes are too pure to look upon evil, and You cannot tolerate wrongdoing. So why do You tolerate the faithless? Why are You silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than themselves?
passages.sermon:
God, You are holy.
Your eyes are pure.
You do not look at evil.
You cannot tolerate wrongdoing.
You do not accept injustice.
Why do You look at those who betray others?
Why do You stay silent?
The wicked destroy people who are more righteous than themselves.
You allow this to happen.
Why do You let the wicked swallow up the righteous?
passages.original: טְה֤וֹר עֵינַ֙יִם֙ מֵרְא֣וֹת רָ֔ע וְהַבִּ֥יט אֶל־ עָמָ֖ל לֹ֣א תוּכָ֑ל לָ֤מָּה תַבִּיט֙ בּֽוֹגְדִ֔ים תַּחֲרִ֕ישׁ בְּבַלַּ֥ע רָשָׁ֖ע צַדִּ֥יק מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: You have made men like the fish of the sea, like creeping things that have no ruler.
passages.sermon:
God made people.
People are like the fish in the sea.
People are also like crawling creatures.
No one rules over these fish or creatures.
People have no ruler over them, just like the fish and the crawling things.
passages.original: וַתַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אָדָ֖ם כִּדְגֵ֣י הַיָּ֑ם כְּרֶ֖מֶשׂ לֹא־ מֹשֵׁ֥ל בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The foe pulls all of them up with a hook; he catches them in his dragnet, and gathers them in his fishing net; so he rejoices gladly.
passages.sermon:
The foe acts with power and cruelty.
He pulls all people up with a hook.
He catches them in his dragnet.
He gathers them in his fishing net.
He rejoices.
He feels glad.
passages.original: כֻּלֹּה֙ בְּחַכָּ֣ה הֵֽעֲלָ֔ה יְגֹרֵ֣הוּ בְחֶרְמ֔וֹ וְיַאַסְפֵ֖הוּ בְּמִכְמַרְתּ֑וֹ עַל־ כֵּ֖ן יִשְׂמַ֥ח וְיָגִֽיל׃

passages.text: Therefore he sacrifices to his dragnet and burns incense to his fishing net, for by these things his portion is sumptuous and his food is rich.
passages.sermon:
The foe is a man who conquers others.
He catches people as if they are fish.
He uses a dragnet and a fishing net to gather them.
He offers sacrifices to his dragnet.
He burns incense to his fishing net.
He does this because these tools give him great wealth.
His portion is rich because of them.
His food is plentiful because of them.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּן֙ יְזַבֵּ֣חַ לְחֶרְמ֔וֹ וִֽיקַטֵּ֖ר לְמִכְמַרְתּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י בָהֵ֙מָּה֙ שָׁמֵ֣ן חֶלְק֔וֹ וּמַאֲכָל֖וֹ בְּרִאָֽה׃

passages.text: Will he, therefore, empty his net and continue to slay nations without mercy?
passages.sermon:
The foe is cruel.
He catches many people in his net.
He destroys nations.
He shows no mercy.
Will he keep emptying his net?
Will he always kill nations without pity?
passages.original: הַ֥עַל כֵּ֖ן יָרִ֣יק חֶרְמ֑וֹ וְתָמִ֛יד לַהֲרֹ֥ג גּוֹיִ֖ם לֹ֥א יַחְמֽוֹל׃ס
